A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chart2Code benchmark. Their text, tables, figures, equations, code listings, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations in Tables 3–5 and 7–16, qualitative experiments, and a human evaluation study in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark measurements and human evaluation, now in Appendix E, and adds qualitative failure analysis in Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: The three-level benchmark and evaluation pipeline using Figure objects and GPT-5-mini are unchanged. The evaluator implementations and generation/evaluation prompts in Appendices L–M match; clarified terminology does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,186 tasks, divided into 863/1,010/313 tasks across the three levels. DR, CRD, and CFD already appear in v2. The additional failure examples concern retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The model rosters in the main and detailed evaluation tables, and the human-comparison model group, are unchanged. Newly discussed ChartBench and BigDocs are related work, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, judges, configuration values in Table 20, difficulty subsets, and human-evaluation sampling remain unchanged. The expanded configuration prose restates existing settings, and the qualitative error study does not establish a changed testing protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds Appendix D.4 and Figures 17–34, substantially expanding failure analysis beyond v2's perception examples and three evaluator case studies. It organizes failures across all levels into color, positioning, data, scale, type, grid, text, and styling errors, alongside editing-specific and long-context cases.

E5.justification: The correlation analyses and human-evaluation reporting retain the same Pearson, Spearman, Kendall, RMSE, and bias measures. Neither version adds different repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores, rankings, and human-evaluation results are retained. v3 adds qualitative failure outcomes supporting previously reported difficulties, and Table 18 changes the reported grid score from 0.13 in v2's explanation to 0.12. Most other case-table numerical differences are disaggregation or precision changes.

T1.justification: The task formulation and mathematical evaluation definitions, including Equations 1–46, are retained from v2 Appendix G in v3 Appendix F. No new theorem, proof, substantive assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: a hierarchical benchmark, complementary evaluation metrics, and an extensive model study revealing difficulties with editing and long-table visualization. The headline numerical claims also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit interpretation that the dominant bottleneck shifts from perception to reasoning and then long-context comprehension, including a lost-in-the-middle explanation. This refines the existing complexity/fidelity account; the English-only and evaluator-bias limitations are retained. The new causal explanations are not established by controlled tests.

D1.justification: The expanded configuration and model-information prose restates information already supplied in v2's tables. Hardware, checkpoints, configuration values, model licenses and sources, dataset-example code, evaluator code, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds ChartBench and BigDocs citations and distinguishes their tasks from Chart2Code. Table 1 adds benchmark sizes, and the task description drops v2's categorical statement that style transfer with data was overlooked by prior studies. Most related-work content is retained and relocated.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to main Section 2, contributions become bullets, task and metric abbreviations receive clearer explanations, and several appendix introductions expand. Dataset examples receive a separate Appendix K. Most existing scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Beyond adding Figures 17–34, v3 substantially reformats existing case studies and dataset examples into larger, full-width displays. Tables 17–19 use paired metric columns, Table 1 gains a dataset-size column, and existing figures and tables are reorganized. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 makes existing examples easier to inspect and adds useful diagnostic coverage through the structured failure analysis in Appendix D.4. Clearer related-work placement and evaluation explanations also help readers. These gains are limited by unspecified model identities in the new failure panels and untested causal explanations; the underlying quantitative evidence and human validation are unchanged.
